Subject: Skyrise security RFI: EU geofencing, retention & deletion

Marcus —

Thanks for taking this. Attached is our short RFI (Skyrise_Security_RFI_v2.pdf). A few high-priority questions to start with so we can triage internally: 

1) Where will Skyrise tenant data (API inputs, call logs, embeddings) be stored by default for the hosted API? We need explicit EU-only residency details.
2) What are default retention TTLs for: (a) request payloads / model inputs, (b) user-level logs / request traces, (c) embeddings and vector indexes derived from inputs, and (d) backup snapshots?
3) For deletion requests: what is the workflow, expected timeline for permanent removal from hot storage, cold snapshots, and backups? How do you provide deletion evidence?
4) Do backups or replication ever leave the EU under normal operation or for disaster recovery?
5) How long is ephemeral runtime state (KV cache / session cache) retained and where is it stored?

Can you provide concise, numbered answers we can paste into our intake sheet this afternoon? If useful, please point us to any evidence links or attach a factsheet.

Appreciate it —
Aisha

Kimberly / Rishi —

Aisha at Skyrise pinged for EU-specific answers. Draft below — can you confirm the technical wording on backups and KV cache? I want to avoid implying any cross-border replication without an explicit opt-in.

Draft answers (short form for their intake sheet):
1) Residency: By default for Skyrise (EU tenant) hosted API traffic and persistent artifacts are pinned to our EU region. All customer-specific data (API inputs, generated outputs, metadata, embeddings) are stored on EU-region hosts.

2) Default retention TTLs:
  a) API inputs / model inputs: default 24 hours ephemeral; we do not persist inputs to long-term storage unless customer enables longer retention for evals or debugging (explicit opt-in).
  b) User-level logs / request traces: 30 days by default (token/latency/cost logs). Longer retention can be configured under contract.
  c) Derived embeddings: 90 days by default for hosted tenants; can be set to shorter or zero by customer.
  d) Backup snapshots: 90 days by default for regional disaster recovery snapshots. Snapshots are encrypted at rest.

3) Deletion process: Tenant-level deletion is initiated via our data deletion API and a documented purge run. Hot storage removal: 48–72 hours. Snapshots & cold backups: scheduled purge windows — typically completed within 30–90 days depending on snapshot schedule. We provide a deletion report (timestamped audit record) on completion.

4) Cross-region replication: By default we do not replicate EU tenant backups outside the EU. Cross-region replication only occurs if explicitly requested in contract (e.g., DR to another region) or for legal obligations.

5) Runtime (KV / cache): Inference KV caches are held in GPU-local memory and ephemeral SSD caches on EU hosts for short-term reuse; they are not written to globally replicated object stores. Ephemeral runtime state is flushed at session close; practical retention is under 24 hours.

Open questions for engineering: is the tenant deletion finality window for snapshots strictly "within 90 days" or should we say "up to 90 days depending on snapshot cadence"? Also confirm phrasing for KV cache: "GPU-local memory + ephemeral SSD on EU hosts, not replicated" — accurate?

If you sign off, I'll send to Aisha with the factsheet attached.

Thanks,
Marcus

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the RFI. Please find concise answers below (we've attached a short factsheet as well). If you need a single-sheet summary we can also provide a downloadable evidence pack and a short call to walk through the controls.

1) Residency (EU):
- By default, tenant data for EU-tagged customers is served and stored on our EU-hosted clusters (no cross-border writes). Persistent artifacts include: API inputs you elect to retain, generated outputs saved by application logic, metadata, and embeddings.

2) Retention (defaults):
- API inputs / model inputs: Ephemeral by default (24 hours). We retain for longer only with explicit customer opt-in for debugging, evals, or product features.
- Request logs / request traces (operational logs): 30 days by default.
- Derived embeddings / vector artifacts: 90 days default; can be configured to 0 days (never stored) or a shorter TTL via account settings.
- Backup snapshots: 90 days default. Snapshots are encrypted with keys managed within the EU region if you select EU-only keys.

3) Deletion workflow & evidence:
- Initiation: Customer may call the tenant-deletion API or ask support to open a delete run.
- Hot storage removal: typically completed within 48–72 hours (immediate purge of active indexes and object store references).
- Snapshots/cold backups: purged according to snapshot lifecycle — typically within 30–90 days depending on snapshot schedule and retention policy.
- Evidence: We generate a timestamped audit report (JSON) listing the deletion job id, affected resources, and completion timestamps; we can share the report via a secure Drive link or upload to your intake ticket.

4) Cross-region replication:
- Default behavior: EU-hosted tenants' backups and snapshots are kept within the EU. Cross-region replication does not occur unless explicitly requested and contracted for (customer-driven DR).

5) Runtime cache (KV / session state):
- KV caches used for inference are stored in GPU-local memory and short-lived ephemeral SSD on the EU hosts. They are designed for performance, are transient in nature, and are not replicated to other regions; typical retention is under 24 hours and they are flushed at the end of a session/instance lifecycle.

Attachments: redwood_residency_factsheet_v1.pdf (short summary), evidence pack available on request: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-evidence-pack-123

Next steps: If you want, we can 1) open a compliance evidence package for your security team, or 2) schedule a 30-minute follow-up to go deeper on snapshot lifecycles and customer-managed KMS options.

Best,
